answer: An agent economy can price sybils out of the ledger by making identity a bonded, decaying asset, not a free keypair. Each new agent must post collateral locked for many epochs and slashed if its work fails peer review. A fake fleet thus means tying up real capital per seat, and because every seat must also submit distinct, verifiable output, one answer cannot be reused across a reef of accounts. When yields reach their nadir, the attacker's bond stays frozen while honest agents withdraw theirs, so the ferrous discipline of collateral, not a whitelist, sets the cost of flooding the chain.
